audit_findings.title: Post-split valuation uses an apparently pre-split share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: computed 50% per-share overstatement; restating 1,004.416 million shares to 2,008.832 million halves bear/base/bull values from $24.49/$28.30/$32.78 to approximately $12.25/$14.15/$16.39 and buy-below from $19.81 to approximately $9.91
audit_findings.mechanism: The stock split doubles the fully diluted share denominator without changing aggregate OE or equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of shares of the registrant’s common stock, $0.005 par value per share (being the only class of common stock of the registrant), outstanding on February 13, 2026 was 978,270,734 shares.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated unit mismatch. The August 2026 filing gives split-adjusted diluted shares of roughly twice the reported pre-split amount, while the September 4 market price is necessarily after split-adjusted trading began. Every supplied per-share valuation output is therefore approximately double its consistent post-split amount. The correction strengthens rather than reverses the conclusion that $44.08 exceeds intrinsic value, but a 50% error in all per-share outputs is valuation-material.
audit_findings.action: Restate every outstanding share, option, RSU, PSU and cover-share input for the two-for-one split, rebuild the fully diluted ceiling, confirm the $44.08 price is post-split, and rerun all per-share scenario and buy-below outputs.

audit_findings.title: Long-term investment principal may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $781.314 million at June 30, 2026; computed 2.75% of the $28.428 billion base equity value, equal to about $0.78 per supplied pre-split share or $0.39 per split-adjusted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Long-term investments belong in the equity bridge when portfolio interest income is removed from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had $2.09 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $677.1 million in short-term investments, and $487.3 million in long-term investments, including commercial paper, certificates of deposit, municipal securities, U.S. treasuries and corporate bonds.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated: the $3.419256 billion bridge amount exactly equals June cash of $2.192424 billion plus short-term investments of $1.226832 billion and excludes the separately filed $781.314 million of long-term investments. Adding it would not approach the gap between the base value and the $44.08 market price and would increase base equity value by only about 2.75%, so this finding alone is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Add the filed June 30 long-term investment balance to the bridge, subject to confirming it is unrestricted and not otherwise represented, and rerun the bridge and per-share outputs.

audit_findings.title: Recurring Alcohol impairments may have been stripped as though one-time
audit_findings.magnitude: filed impairment charges of $53.7 million in 2025 and $138.8 million in 2024; respectively 3.0% of 2025 OE and 9.6% of 2024 OE; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any impairment add-back raises historical OE and potentially the trend-derived anchor and growth assessment despite recurring economic losses in Alcohol Brands.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating expenses for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, included impairment charges of $53.7 million and $138.8 million, respectively, related to the Alcohol Brands segment.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurring impairment and operating-loss evidence is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE schedules added the charges back or how acquisition, abandonment and replacement costs were normalized. The possible distortion could affect the anchor because the charges are meaningful relative to annual OE, but its actual valuation impact cannot be established without the reconciliations.
audit_findings.action: Inspect each judged-year OE reconciliation for impairment add-backs; if present, rerun the anchor and scenarios with a documented normalized economic cost for Alcohol Brands, including recurring acquisition, replacement or abandonment losses.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-revenue releases can double count cash already received
audit_findings.magnitude: filed revenue recognition of approximately $40.0 million annually; filed deferred-revenue cash-flow reductions of $24.472 million in 2023, $17.360 million in 2024, $23.005 million in 2025 and $6.475 million in the first half of 2026; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining noncash revenue releases in OE while also adding the original cash in the bridge inflates OE, and perpetuating the release can inflate growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, $ 40.0 million, $ 39.9 million and $ 40.0 million, respectively, of deferred revenue, was recognized in net sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The releases and continuing balance runoff are demonstrated. The cash-flow statements record changes in deferred revenue, which would prevent double counting if those adjustments flowed correctly into OE, but the supplied valuation lacks the yearly OE reconciliations needed to verify that treatment. The roughly $40 million annual release is 2.25% of the $1.7799 billion anchor, yet erroneous terminal perpetuation could compound its effect, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace deferred-revenue changes with the correct sign through every OE year and rerun the forecast excluding releases unsupported by new cash receipts, including the terminal period.

audit_findings.title: Repatriation-tax claims may not be netted against gross cash
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $10.0 million at December 31, 2025; computed 0.035% of base equity value and about $0.01 per supplied pre-split share or $0.005 per split-adjusted share
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid repatriation-tax liability reduces the net cash available in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the Company had a deferred tax liability of $ 10.0 million for the estimated taxes associated with the repatriation of these earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the liability remained outstanding at June 30 or was otherwise captured is unresolved, but even deducting the entire filed $10 million would change the $28.428 billion base equity value by only about 0.035%. That scale cannot reasonably change the valuation conclusion relative to the $44.08 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 30 foreign-cash tax liability and deduct any unpaid amount from the equity bridge; no full valuation rerun is necessary unless a materially larger associated tax claim is identified.
